about.heading: About
about.body: YGO Omega is an automatic (and manual) Yu-Gi-Oh Trading Card Game simulator developed by Duelists Unite (DU). It has all of the cards for free with an automatic Swiss Tournament system and ranking. The DU discord hosts weekly tournaments with prizes and even casual players with beginner knowledge of Yu-Gi-Oh can find something to enjoy!

Tiers and the Top win rate order use the adjusted win rate, shrunk toward the ladder and widened by each deck's day-to-day swing, so a small sample can't top the list on a hot streak; the win rates shown are raw.

method.title: How it’s counted
method.body: Each game counts once per deck, so a Bo3 adds up to six deck-games. Win rates leave out mirrors and unfinished games; a draw counts as a game, not a win. Meta share keeps everything. Decks with fewer than {minSamples} deck-games are left out of the lists, so shares don’t add up to 100%. Unknown decks count in the totals, not as a row. ± is the 95% Wilson interval of the raw rate. Adjusted: the rate pulled toward the ladder's mean by a prior fitted on the ladder (a deck with few games sits near the mean) and widened by φ, how much its daily rate moves beyond pure chance; the games of one Bo3 and of one pilot are not independent, so φ runs about 1.5. Tier: how far a deck's adjusted rate sits below the best deck's (T1 and T1.5 up to 1 point, T1 for the best two only; T2 up to 3, T3 up to 6, T4 up to 9; none under 0.5% of the meta or 10 players). Read with care: after game 1 the loser picks who goes first, so the first-turn edge in games 2–3 is diluted by who was already behind; a card's win rate when used is conditioned on drawing it with a target, so a hand trap used in losing spots reads low; a deck whose games come from a handful of duelists carries their skill.

overview.tierRule: A deck's tier is how far its adjusted win rate sits from the best deck's. Popularity doesn't count: a deck with a small share can be Tier 1.
overview.tierBands: T1 and T1.5 · within {t1} point, T1 for the best two · T2 · {t2} points · T3 · {t3} · T4 · {t4} · needs {share}% of the meta and {players} duelists
overview.byRatingNote: Share of deck-games inside each rating tier. Tiers with fewer than 100 duelists join the tier below.
overview.pilotsNote: Share of the deck's games played by its 5 busiest duelists. Past 25%, a few specialists can move the numbers.
overview.tierHistoryNote: Tier over a rolling 7-day window, so one quiet day doesn't move it.
overview.hoursMeta: Ranked matches started per hour · in your time zone
overview.hoursLabel: Ranked matches started per hour, your time zone. Busiest: {hour}:00.
overview.eventsNote: Share moves of 2+ points or win rate moves of 5+ points that pass a two-proportion test at z 4.2: what survives a correction for the hundreds of windows checked.

ranking.title: Deck ranking
ranking.legend: Win rate is raw, ± 95% CI · Adjusted = shrunk toward the ladder, widened by the deck's day-to-day swing · {days}-day = share points vs the {days} days before: half the synced days, 7 at most
ranking.searchDown: The deck search isn't available right now. Try again in a moment.

note.mostPlayed: Sorted by meta share. {days}-day = share points against the {days} days before.
note.highestWinRate: Sorted by the adjusted win rate, so a hot streak on few games doesn't top the list; decks with fewer than 10 duelists stay out. The win rate column stays raw.
note.rising: Popularity: share points, the last {days} days against the {days} days before. Performance: win rate points over the same windows, weighted by games. Trajectory compares this window's change with the previous one.
note.sleeper: A hidden gem is under {share} of the meta, has {games}+ games and an adjusted win rate at or above the meta median. The list holds only those decks.
note.consistent: Stability is the standard deviation of the daily win rate, weighted by games, over at least {days} days. Decks with a typical win rate under 50% stay out.
note.consistentNoise: Variation is φ: how much the daily win rate moves beyond what pure chance would, 1.0 being chance alone (Bo3 games and the same pilots repeat, so most decks sit near 1.5). Smallest φ first, then the adjusted win rate, over at least {days} days. Decks with a typical win rate under 50% stay out.
